title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: genus 0, three points. Let pi_{0,3} = <l_0,l_1,l_inf | l_inf l_1 l_0 = 1> be the free group of rank 2, the fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,inf}. Let G = 𝔖_{0,3} = Aut_loc(pi_{0,3}) be the 'local' automorphisms: those sending each l_i to a conjugate of some l_j^{±1}. These are the automorphisms induced by lifting automorphisms of the punctured sphere to the universal cover, including orientation-reversing ones. Since pi_{0,3} has trivial centre, G is an extension 1 -> pi_{0,3} (inner automorphisms) -> G -> T_{0,3} = S_3 x Z/2 -> 1. Here T_{0,3} has order 12; it is generated by the S_3 of Moebius permutations of 0,1,inf and by complex conjugation tau. Classically G^+ is PSL_2(Z) acting on the upper half plane, the normaliser of Gamma(2), and G is PGL_2(Z), though the page does not say this.

The page writes explicit lifts of all the torsion elements of T_{0,3}, so as to have a calculus in G.

(14) Lifts of the stabiliser S'_3 of the pole -j-bar:
- rho: l_0 -> l_1 -> l_inf -> l_0.
- tau'_0: l_0 -> l_0^{-1}, l_1 <-> l_inf^{-1}; tau'_1 and tau'_inf are defined similarly. These are orientation-reversing.

(15) These form an honest subgroup isomorphic to S_3 of Aut(pi_{0,3}): tau'_0 tau'_1 = tau'_1 tau'_inf = tau'_inf tau'_0 = rho. Each tau'_i has order 2 and rho^3 = 1. So the projection splits over S'_3.

(16) Orientation-preserving involutions sigma_i lifting the transpositions:
- sigma_0 swaps l_1 and l_inf and sends l_0 to (l_1 l_inf)^{-1} = l_1 l_0 l_1^{-1}.
- sigma_1 and sigma_inf are obtained cyclically.

(17) Conjugation by rho permutes the sigma_i cyclically, and likewise the tau_i.

(18) The products sigma_i sigma_{i+1} equal rho composed with an inner automorphism. For example sigma_0 sigma_1 = rho·int(l_0) = int(l_1)·rho. This is the failure of the sigma's to form a splitting over S_3.

(19)-(20) Lifts of complex conjugation tau: tau_i := sigma_i tau'_i = tau'_i sigma_i. Each tau_i is characterised as the lift of tau that has order 2 and commutes with sigma_i. Concretely, tau_0 inverts l_1 and l_inf and sends l_0 to l_1 l_inf.

(21) tau_inf tau_1 = l_0, tau_0 tau_inf = l_1, tau_1 tau_0 = l_inf, read as inner automorphisms. Hence pi_{0,3} ⋊ <tau> is generated by three involutions whose pairwise products are the loops. This is the reflection group of the ideal hyperbolic triangle, isomorphic to Z/2*Z/2*Z/2: the three real intervals give the three non-conjugate real structures (lifts of tau), as stated on the next page.

The page ends by noting that one should make explicit the geometric (cellular) description of all these elements, referring to Malgoire.

Purpose: this sets up a hand calculus for the extended Teichmüller group Gamma_{0,3}, presumably as input to the 'équation des lacets' (the relations a Galois/GT-type action must satisfy on F_2). The next page continues with square roots epsilon_i of l_i and the classification of torsion lifts mod pi-conjugacy via fixed-point components.
errors: Third relation of (18): the page appears to read sigma_inf sigma_0 = rho l_inf = l_0 rho^{-1}. The correct value is rho·int(l_inf) = int(rho(l_inf))·rho = int(l_0)·rho. The exponent -1 on rho is a slip, or a misreading of the manuscript.
Formula numbering is reused: (21) also appears on the next page with different content. This is harmless.

All other formulas (14)-(17), (19)-(21) check out by direct computation. That includes the relation-preservation checks, tau'_i tau'_j = rho exactly (not merely up to inner automorphisms), sigma_0 sigma_1 = rho·int(l_0), tau_0^2 = 1, [tau_0, sigma_0] = 1 and tau_1 tau_0 = int(l_inf).

ideas.what: Aut_loc(pi_{0,3}) as an extension of S_3 x Z/2 by the free group, with explicit lifts of all torsion elements
ideas.modern_name: extended mapping class / Teichmüller group of the thrice-punctured sphere, isomorphic to PGL_2(Z) (oriented part isomorphic to PSL_2(Z) = normaliser of Gamma(2))
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Fricke-Klein); in the anabelian/GT setting Grothendieck, Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak-Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses Gamma_{0,3} and the Teichmüller tower in general terms; the explicit formulas are presumably in La Longue Marche (circulated)

ideas.what: Three lifts tau_0, tau_1, tau_inf of complex conjugation with tau_j tau_i equal to the loops l_k
ideas.modern_name: reflection group of the ideal triangle, pi_1 ⋊ Z/2 ≅ Z/2*Z/2*Z/2; real structures / real points of M_{0,4} and the 'tangential base points on real intervals'

ideas.what: The S_3 of tau'_i and rho is an honest splitting over the stabiliser of the pole, whereas the sigma_i satisfy sigma_i sigma_{i+1} = rho·(inner)
ideas.modern_name: torsion elements of PSL_2(Z) / PGL_2(Z) and their conjugacy classes (fixed points of elliptic elements)

ideas.what: Characterisation of a torsion lift by commutation conditions, with lifts mod conjugacy classified by components of fixed-point sets in the universal cover (next page)
ideas.modern_name: conjugacy classes of finite subgroups of mapping class groups vs fixed points in Teichmüller space (Kerckhoff/Nielsen realisation in this trivial case)

deep.surprise_reason: These are correct, careful but classical computations in PGL_2(Z) ≅ Aut_loc(F_2), written as preparatory bookkeeping for the 'loop equation'. Nothing here goes beyond what is standard in the GT / Teichmüller-tower literature.
transcription_corrections: Third relation of (18): the transcription has 'l_0 rho^{-1}'; mathematically it should be 'l_0 rho', so check the manuscript, which may well read the same slip.
First line: the crossed-out start '(14) = rho(l_0)=' is a struck draft, not content.
In the line 'On identifie ces éléments à des éléments du groupe Aut_loc(pi_{0,3}) ≃ 𝔖_{0,3}', the following line defines the action of g ∈ 𝔖'_3 on x ∈ pi_{0,3} by g(x) = g x g^{-1} ('on trouve').
